title: Tutorial Tours run as a modal on whatever screen you are on and tell you to click tabs that are not there -- and the modal blocks every one of them
what_happened: Settings > Help & Tutorials > Tutorial Tours > Equipment Setup > Start opens a centred modal dialog with a full-screen scrim, ON THE SETTINGS SCREEN. Step 1 reads 'Equipment Profiles -- Click the Profiles tab to manage your equipment configurations.' There is no Profiles tab on the Settings screen, and the scrim swallows clicks so the user cannot go find one: with the overlay up I clicked the left-nav 'Imaging' entry (root 240,350) and the app stayed on Settings with the overlay unchanged. All 4 steps behave the same way ('Click the Connections tab', 'Check the status indicators for each device') -- it is a slideshow of instructions about a screen you are not on and cannot navigate to.
expected: Starting a tutorial should route to the screen the tutorial is about (Equipment) and spotlight the real control, or at minimum let the underlying UI stay clickable so the instruction can be followed. NINA/SGP tours anchor to the widget being described.
repro: Fresh profile > skip onboarding > gear icon > Help & Tutorials > scroll to Tutorial Tours > Equipment Setup 'Start'. Observe the modal appears over Settings. Click left-nav Imaging: nothing happens.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-05.png (modal 'Equipment Profiles / Click the Profiles tab' rendered over the Settings > Help page), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-06.png (step 3 'Click the Connections tab'). Tree after clicking left-nav Imaging still reports the Settings panel plus 'Tutorial step 1 of 4: Equipment Profiles'.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/help_tutorials_settings.dart:179 (onStart -> notifier.restartTutorial) and packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/tutorial_provider.dart:640 _restartTutorial -- it only sets state.activeCategory/currentStepIndex, it never navigates.
proposed_fix: Give TutorialStep a target route and have _restartTutorial/resumeTutorial push it before showing step 0; make the overlay a non-blocking anchored coach-mark rather than a modal barrier.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live (display :83, profile v2-settings-system). Settings > Help & Tutorials > Tutorial Tours > Equipment Setup > Start renders a centred modal with a full-screen scrim ON the Settings screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-05.png). Step 1 reads 'Equipment Profiles / Click the Profiles tab...' and there is no Profiles tab on Settings. With the overlay up I clicked the left-nav 'Imaging' entry; the tree afterwards still reported 'Tutorial step 1 of 4: Equipment Profiles [DISABLED]' over Settings > Help & Tutorials, so the scrim swallowed the click and no navigation happened. Cited locations check out: help_tutorials_settings.dart:179-180 onStart -> notifier.restartTutorial(equipmentSetup); tutorial_provider.dart:640 _restartTutorial only sets activeCategory/currentStepIndex and never routes. Extra observation: the row still reads 'Not started' while the tour is running.

title: Remote Access claims 'Localhost stays frictionless for this machine' -- localhost is not exempt from auth at all
what_happened: With Enable Remote Access on, the page's footer note reads 'Localhost stays frictionless for this machine, while non-local clients must pair before they can control the app', the 'Open on this computer' card says 'Use this link from the same machine to confirm the dashboard is working before sharing it elsewhere', and Connection details reports Authentication = 'Paired devices required remotely'. All three say local is special. It is not: from 127.0.0.1, GET /api/status -> 401 {'error':'Authentication required','message':'Missing Authorization header or session cookie'}; so do /api/images/recent, /api/auth/csrf and POST /api/auth/cookie. The bytes returned to 127.0.0.1 and to 192.168.1.20 are identical 401s. Only the static /dashboard shell is 200, and it can load no data. The auth middleware has no loopback branch at all.
expected: Either implement the documented loopback exemption (peer address is loopback -> full-scope identity), or change the copy so it does not promise a local escape hatch that does not exist. As written, an operator clicking 'Open Local Dashboard' to 'confirm the dashboard is working' sees a dead page and concludes the server is broken.
repro: Settings > Remote Access > Enable Remote Access. Then: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/status -> 401. curl http://localhost:<port>/api/status -> 401. curl http://192.168.1.20:<port>/api/status -> 401.
evidence: Live 401 bodies captured from 127.0.0.1:8080 and 127.0.0.1:8099 (both ports I ran on). /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-20.png shows the 'Open on this computer' copy, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-19.png shows Connection details.
where: copy: packages/skotiq_app/lib/localization/skotiq_localizations/translations.dart:389 and :399; enforcement: apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/http_middleware.dart:758-770 (token==null -> 401, no peer-address check anywhere in the chain).
proposed_fix: Add an explicit loopback grant in the auth middleware keyed on the shelf connectionInfo remote address (and NOT on any forwarded header), or drop the 'frictionless' sentence and relabel the card 'Open the dashboard (you will need to pair this browser)'.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Enabled remote access on port 8391 (ss shows 0.0.0.0:8391). From 127.0.0.1: /api/status -> 401 {'error':'Authentication required','message':'Missing Authorization header or session cookie'}; /api/images/recent -> 401; /api/auth/csrf -> 401; /api/system/info -> 401. Only GET /dashboard is 200 (static shell). All three copy strings are still live: the footer note, the 'Open on this computer / Use this link from the same machine to confirm the dashboard is working' card, and Connection details -> Authentication 'Paired devices required remotely' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-15.png). Locations check out: translations.dart:389 remoteAccessInfoBody and :398-399 remoteAccessLocalActionTitle/Body; http_middleware.dart has no peer-address branch anywhere in the auth chain (its only 'loopback' mentions concern the rate-limit trusted-proxy header and CORS) and the token==null -> 401 return at :759-771 fires regardless of peer.

title: After a device pairs successfully the desktop keeps showing the pairing code counting down, and the device list does not update
what_happened: I pressed Start Pairing Mode, read the code ASTRO-NEBULA-1815 off the screen, and completed pairing over HTTP (POST /api/pairing/verify -> 200 with a bearer token). The server immediately invalidated the code (a second verify with the same code returned invalid_pairing_code) and wrote the 13th row into paired_devices. The desktop screen did not react at all: 30s later it still displayed 'Enter this code on your device: ASTRO-NEBULA-1815 / Expires in 04:18 / Cancel Pairing', and Paired Devices still listed 12 entries. Only after manually pressing the small refresh icon did the 13th device appear.
expected: The instant a code is consumed the panel should close and announce which device paired -- that confirmation is the operator's only way to know the phone in their hand is the device that just connected. Showing a live countdown for a code the server has already destroyed is a false statement, and it invites the operator to read the dead code to a second device.
repro: Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing > Start Pairing Mode. From a shell: curl -X POST -d '{"code":"<code>","deviceName":"x","deviceId":"x","deviceType":"browser"}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/pairing/verify. Watch the desktop: unchanged. sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) from paired_devices where is_active=1' -> 13 while the UI shows 12.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-23.png (code panel), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-24.png (still counting down at 04:03 after the pair completed). Tree: 12 'Paired:' rows vs DB 13. After pressing refresh: 13 rows, 'audit-probe ... Paired: 1m ago'.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/pairing_screen.dart:96/215 (loadPairedDevices is only called on init and on the manual refresh button; nothing subscribes to pairing completion).
proposed_fix: Have the pairing session emit a completion event (the server already knows) and drive the panel from it: close the code card, toast '<deviceName> paired', and reload the list.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Manage Pairing > Start Pairing Mode; code NEBULA-MOON-4612. POST /api/pairing/verify -> 200 with a bearer token; a second verify with the same code -> 401 invalid_pairing_code, so the server destroyed it immediately, and paired_devices went 13 -> 14 active rows. The desktop did not react: at +5s and again at +60s the tree still read 'Enter this code on your device: / Expires in 04:35 ... 04:18 / Cancel Pairing', and the list rendered 13 'Paired:' rows against the DB's 14. Location is right: pairing_screen.dart:94-96 _initialize() is the constructor-time load, :215 loadPairedDevices, and the only other caller is the manual refresh IconButton at :484 -- nothing subscribes to pairing completion.

title: Paired devices always say 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet' -- last_connected_at is never written
what_happened: Every one of the 13 paired devices shows the badge 'Not seen yet' and the line 'No connection recorded yet'. I proved this is untrue for at least one of them: after pairing 'audit-probe' I made three authenticated GET /api/status calls with its bearer (200, 200, 200) and then opened an authenticated WebSocket to /events (HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols, held open 60s). paired_devices.last_connected_at for that device stayed NULL and the UI still says 'Not seen yet'. All 12 pre-existing devices -- including ones that demonstrably drove this app in earlier sessions ('ui-audit-avd', 'Lead Harness') -- are likewise NULL.
expected: last_connected_at should be stamped whenever a device authenticates. Without it the operator cannot tell a phone that is still in use from a stale credential, which makes the revoke list unusable: 7 of the 13 rows are named 'Android companion' with identical subtitles and no last-seen, IP or model to tell them apart.
repro: Pair a device via POST /api/pairing/verify, call GET /api/status with the returned bearer (200), then sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db "select device_name,last_connected_at from paired_devices where device_id='audit-probe-rss'" -> last_connected_at empty. Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing > refresh: row still reads 'No connection recorded yet'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-24.png (every row 'Not seen yet'); SQL output showing NULL last_connected_at for all 13 rows; curl 200s and the 101 upgrade transcript.
where: packages/skotiq_remote_protocol/lib/src/database/pairing_database.dart (no update of last_connected_at on the auth path) / apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/http_middleware.dart token resolution.
proposed_fix: Stamp last_connected_at (throttled, e.g. at most once a minute per device) when a bearer resolves, and surface it plus the peer IP in the device row.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. After pairing device_id v2-probe-adv I made three authenticated GET /api/status calls with its bearer (200, 200, 200) and held an authenticated WebSocket on /events (101 Switching Protocols, ESTAB in ss for minutes). sqlite3 on the scratch pairing.db shows last_connected_at NULL for v2-probe-adv and for all 13 other rows, and every UI row reads 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet'. Root cause is slightly more precise than stated: the write exists (pairing_database.dart:138 updateLastConnected) and its only non-test caller is token_manager.dart:297 inside TokenManager.verifySessionToken, which the HTTP auth path never calls -- the desktop server authenticates from its in-memory BoundedTokenGrantMap _pairedSessionTokens (declared headless_api_server.dart:233, hydrated at server_lifecycle.dart:366, compared at http_middleware.dart:1030), so no request ever reaches the stamping code.

title: 'Active Viewers' on the Remote Access page counts co-imaging collaborators, not connected remote clients -- it stays 0 with a live dashboard socket open
what_happened: Connection details is introduced as 'Open this section when you need viewer counts, authentication state, or the last runtime error' and shows 'Active Viewers'. With a paired client holding an authenticated WebSocket on /events (verified: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols, socket ESTAB in ss for the whole window) the panel read 'Active Viewers 0' throughout. The field is only ever set from the collaboration manager's viewer list (desktop_app_bootstrap.dart:346-349 -> collabState.viewers.length), i.e. co-imaging participants, not remote-access clients. The same field drives the status-bar 'N viewers connected' chip, so that indicator is dead for ordinary phone/browser clients too.
expected: On the Remote Access page 'Active Viewers' must mean 'remote clients currently connected to this server'. Count the live event-stream/WS sessions; if the co-imaging number is wanted too, label it separately.
repro: Enable remote access, pair a client, POST /api/ws/ticket, connect ws to /events?ticket=..., hold. Settings > Remote Access > Connection details: Active Viewers 0.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-28.png ('Active Viewers 0') captured while ss showed the ESTAB pair on :8099 and the probe had logged '101 Switching Protocols'.
proposed_fix: Publish a connected-client count from the headless API server's WS/SSE registry into webServerStateProvider and bind the row to that.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. With a paired client holding an authenticated WebSocket on /events (101 Switching Protocols; ss shows the ESTAB pair on :8391 for the whole window) Connection details read 'Active Viewers 0' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-15.png). Code makes it structural: web_server_provider.dart:193 setActiveViewers is the only mutator of WebServerState.activeViewers, and its only non-test call site is desktop_app_bootstrap.dart:348 inside a listener on nextServer.collaborationManager.stream assigning collabState.viewers.length -- CollaborationViewer is the co-imaging participant type (live_collaboration_session.dart:69). The same field drives the status-bar chip (status_bar/session_sharing.dart:19,70,177-203). All three cited locations are accurate.

title: Deleting your last equipment profile leaves a ghost profile on screen whose 'Set Active' throws an unhandled exception and does nothing
what_happened: Settings > Equipment Profiles with exactly one profile ('Audit Rig Alpha'): overflow > Delete > Delete. equipment_profiles goes to 0 rows and the list column correctly reads 'No profiles yet' -- but the detail pane on the right keeps rendering the deleted profile in full (name, f/8.0, gain 100, all four filters, focus offsets) with a live 'Set Active' button and a live overflow menu. Two surfaces in the same screen disagree about whether the profile exists. Clicking 'Set Active' produces no toast, no error, no visible change: it throws [ERROR] Unhandled Exception: Bad state: Cannot activate profile 1: no such profile row (activateProfileStrictTransactional) straight into the log. Clicking Edit puts the ghost into an editable form; typing a new name and pressing Save shows 'Failed to save profile: Exception: Profile not found' and the typed work is lost.
expected: Deleting the selected profile must clear the selection when nothing is left -- the pane should fall back to the 'Select a profile / Choose a profile from the list or create a new one' empty state (which the app already has and shows before the first profile is created). No control should remain that acts on a deleted row, and a failed activation must never be an unhandled exception.
repro: Fresh profile > Settings > Equipment Profiles > New Profile 'X' > Create > overflow (three dots) > Delete > Delete. Observe list 'No profiles yet' + full detail pane still shown. Click 'Set Active'. sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select count(*) from equipment_profiles' -> 0. drive_linux.py log -> Unhandled Exception: Bad state: Cannot activate profile 1: no such profile row.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-55.png -- middle column reads 'No profiles yet' while the right pane renders 'Audit Rig Alpha' with Set Active. Log lines quoted above; DB count 0 before and after the Set Active click.
proposed_fix: In the profiles notifier, null out the selected profile when the deleted id is the selected one and the list is empty; guard the detail pane on 'selected profile still exists in state.profiles'; wrap _activateProfile in a try/catch that surfaces the failure as a snackbar.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. With exactly one profile left, overflow > Delete > Delete drove equipment_profiles to 0 rows (sqlite3 confirmed) and the middle column correctly showed 'No profiles yet' -- while the right pane kept rendering the deleted profile in full (name, f/5.0, 530 mm, 106 mm, both filters, focus offsets) with a live 'Set Active' button and a live overflow menu (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-36.png). Clicking Set Active produced no toast and no visible change; the log carries the claimed unhandled exception with a stack trace matching all three cited locations verbatim: 'Unhandled Exception: Bad state: Cannot activate profile 6: no such profile row (strict activation requires an existing target)' at profile_activation_writethrough.dart:156 <- profiles_provider.dart:980 _activateProfile <- screen_shell.dart:232. Not separately re-tested this pass: the Edit-then-Save 'Profile not found' half of the report.

title: A profile saved without optics can never be edited again: Save is rejected because of the 0 the app itself stored, and the rejection is invisible on screen
what_happened: New Profile writes focal_length=0.0 / aperture=0.0. Re-open that profile, press Edit, change ONLY the name, press Save: nothing happens. No banner, no field-level error, no colour change -- the button appears dead. I clicked Save five times over three minutes and the DB never changed (still 'Backup Test Rig' while the field read 'Local Work Do Not Lose'). The failure is real and has a message -- the accessibility tree at that moment contains 'Focal length must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)' and 'Aperture must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)' -- but a full-window screenshot taken between the click and that tree read shows no such text anywhere on screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png), and neither does a full-resolution capture of the bottom 160px where the snackbar would sit (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-snack-1.png). The snackbar is rendered underneath the persistent bottom status bar. Clearing both optics fields let the save through -- and it stored 0.0 again, so the profile is right back in the unsavable state next time.
expected: Blank optics must round-trip as blank/NULL, not as 0.0 that the validator then rejects; and a rejected save must show its reason where the user is looking (inline under the offending field, plus a visible banner). As shipped, the very first thing a user does after creating a profile -- open it and fill something in -- hits a dead Save button with no explanation.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > New Profile > name 'X' > Create. Overflow menu > Edit > change the name > Save. Nothing happens; sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select name,focal_length,aperture from equipment_profiles' still shows the old name and 0.0/0.0. Now clear Focal Length and Aperture and press Save: it saves, and stores 0.0/0.0 again.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-64.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png (identical -- edit form with 'Local Work Do Not Lose' typed, Focal Length 0, Aperture 0, no error visible) taken immediately after the Save click; tree read after that same click contains the two validation strings; DB unchanged across all attempts.
where: validator: ProfileValidator.parseOptional... (focal/aperture 'must be a positive number') reached from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_details.dart:175-200; the empty-field -> 0.0 write is in the same save path; the snackbar is shown by the settings scaffold underneath the app's bottom status bar.
location_wrong: profile_details.dart:175-200 -- the optics validators are actually at :170 and :172, the error is raised at :219, and the whole _validateAndBuild is :167-248
proposed_fix: Persist blank optics as NULL (the column is already nullable in the export -- focalLength shows as a number only when set), treat 0 as 'unset' on read, and render validation failures inline on the fields plus a banner above the status bar.
verdict_reasoning: SYMPTOM CONFIRMED, HALF THE STATED CAUSE REFUTED. Confirmed: New Profile wrote id=1 focal_length=0.0 aperture=0.0; the Edit form pre-fills both optics fields with a literal '0'; changing only the name and pressing Save left the DB untouched across repeated attempts; clearing BOTH optics fields let the save through and stored 0.0/0.0 again, putting the profile straight back in the rejecting state. Code is exact: _parseOptic (equipment_profile_validation.dart) returns ok(0.0) for blank but fails any value <= 0 with 'must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)', while the model stores blank as the 0 sentinel and the editor renders that sentinel as '0'. REFUTED: 'nothing happens, no banner, the button appears dead, a full-window screenshot shows no such text'. Burst capture (250 ms interval, numpy diff vs baseline) shows a full-width red SnackBar carrying both messages appearing ~0.5 s after the click and persisting for its 4 s duration. The earlier screenshot was taken inside the entrance-animation latency. The finding IS right that there is no field-level error and no colour change on the offending fields. Downgraded to P2: the user gets a visible banner naming the exact fix, so this is a round-trip trap, not silent failure.

title: The desktop app can never tell you a new version exists: the only 'Updates' page in Settings is for a remote appliance, and the built-in update manager is wired to a server URL nothing ever sets
what_happened: Searching Settings for 'update' returns exactly two entries: About and 'Appliance Updates'. Appliance Updates says 'Connect to a remote appliance to manage its updates. The local desktop app updates itself through its own installer.' and renders nothing else off-network. There is no local update check anywhere in Settings, and About (which the settings catalog even tags with the keyword 'updates') shows only a version string and three web links. The app does ship an in-app updater -- app.dart:204-206 wraps the desktop shell in UpdateManagerWidget, which fires _checkForUpdates() 3 s after launch -- but that check is gated on state.updateServerUrl being non-empty (update_manager_widget.dart:40-43) and the only caller of UpdateNotifier.configure(serverUrl:) in the whole repo is apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/update_wiring.dart, i.e. the appliance server, never the GUI. So on the shipped desktop build the updater is inert: I ran the app for ~40 minutes with working internet and it made no version request, showed no update UI, and logged nothing about updates. The sentence 'updates itself through its own installer' is also not true of the Linux build, which is distributed as a tarball with no installer.
expected: A 'Check for updates' row in About or a Software Update section: current version + build, channel (stable/beta), last checked, and a manual check. NINA and SGP both check at launch and show release notes; an astrophotographer needs to know a fix landed before the night, not after.
repro: Settings > search 'update' -> About, Appliance Updates. Open Appliance Updates on the desktop build: one explanatory sentence, no controls. Open About: version 6.1.0, three links, System Information. No update control anywhere. drive_linux.py log over the whole session contains no update/version request.
evidence: tree of Settings > Appliance Updates (title, subtitle 'Check for, stage, and apply updates to the connected rig', single info panel). Source: packages/skotiq_app/lib/app.dart:204-206, packages/skotiq_updater/lib/src/widgets/update_manager_widget.dart:40-52, packages/skotiq_updater/lib/src/services/update_service.dart:236-239 ('Update server URL not configured'), and grep showing update_wiring.dart:79 as the sole configure() caller.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/update_settings.dart (appliance-only page) and the unconfigured desktop path above
proposed_fix: Configure the update service with the public release feed on desktop startup and give Settings > About a 'Software Update' block (version+build, channel, Check now, last checked). Until that exists, drop the 'updates itself through its own installer' claim.
verdict_reasoning: Live: Settings search 'update' returns exactly About and Appliance Updates. Appliance Updates renders only a title, the subtitle 'Check for, stage, and apply updates to the connected rig' and one info panel 'Connect to a remote appliance to manage its updates. The local desktop app updates itself through its own installer.' -- no controls. About renders version 6.1.0, tagline, three links and System Information; no update control, no build number. Code confirms the dead path at the cited lines: app.dart:204-206 wraps the desktop shell in UpdateManagerWidget; update_manager_widget.dart:39-43 _isUpdateConfigured() and :163-168 _checkForUpdates return early when updateProvider.state.updateServerUrl is empty; the only configure() caller outside the updater package is headless_api/update_wiring.dart:79, reached from desktop_app_bootstrap.dart:377, which builds a SEPARATE UpdateService for the headless API server and needs SKOTIQ_UPDATE_SERVER -- it never touches the Riverpod updateProvider the GUI widget reads.

title: The in-app Logs viewer records nothing about the failures the user just watched happen -- five failed catalog downloads and every rejected save are absent from it and from the 18.8 MB log export
what_happened: Settings > Logs is the surface a user is told to use ('View application logs with filtering and export'). In a session where I triggered the GLADE+ download five times and watched it fail five times, searching the viewer for 'download' gives '0 of 139 entries / No entries match current filters' and searching for 'glade' gives 0 as well. The level filter reports the whole session as one error: Error+ = '1 of 139 entries', the single [ProfileActivationWriteThrough] 'Strict activation aborted: target profile 1 does not exist'. Not logged anywhere: the catalog download failure, the two rejected profile imports, the rejected profile saves, or the two later unhandled 'Cannot activate profile' exceptions that Flutter printed to stderr. I then pressed Export, which produced /home/scdouglas/Documents/skotiq_logs_2026-08-02T11-08-20.txt -- 18,829,614 bytes, 142,921 lines, concatenating the rotated on-disk logs back to 2026-07-27 -- and grepped it: 0 occurrences of 'glade' and 0 of 'annotation catalog download'. The failure genuinely has no persistent record.
expected: Every user-visible failure should leave a log line at WARN/ERROR with the cause (here: the VizieR TAP 503). Otherwise the log viewer gives a user and a support engineer false confidence -- 'only 1 error all night' -- about a session that failed repeatedly.
repro: Settings > Catalogs > Download Standard (~50 MB), which fails. Then Settings > Logs > search 'download' -> 0 of N entries. Set the level filter to Error+ -> 1 of N. Press Export and grep the resulting file for 'glade' -> 0 hits.
evidence: Tree readings '0 of 139 entries / No entries match current filters' for both 'download' and 'glade'; '1 of 139 entries' at Error+ with the single ProfileActivationWriteThrough row; grep -ic glade on the 18.8 MB export -> 0.
where: the catalog download handler in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/catalog_settings_screen.dart (catches and snackbars without logging) and the equivalent swallow in the profile save/import paths
proposed_fix: Log every caught user-facing exception at ERROR with the underlying cause before showing the snackbar.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed on this session's own failures, with one correction to the specifics. This run produced three user-visible 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: ...' snackbars, two rejected profile saves, one unhandled 'Cannot activate profile 6' exception and one successful 15.6 MB GLADE+ download. Settings > Logs then reported: 'duplicat' -> 0 of 124 entries; 'download' -> 0 of 124; 'glade' -> 0 of 124; 'catalog' -> 1; 'profile' -> 2. The only error-level line for the whole session is '[ProfileActivationWriteThrough] Strict activation aborted: target profile 6 does not exist' -- exactly the shape reported. I then pressed Export and grepped the 19,489,798-byte / 147,939-line result: 0 'glade', 0 'duplicat', 0 'annotation catalog'. Mechanism matches the cited location: catalog_settings_screen.dart:1229-1230 catches and calls _showError, which is only context.showErrorSnackBar (:414-418) with no logger call; the duplicate handler does the same at screen_shell.dart:394. Correction: the catalog download SUCCEEDED this time and still produced no log entry, so the gap is 'no catalog-download logging at all, success or failure', not only the failure path.

title: Duplicate reports 'Duplicate profile failed' for a duplicate that succeeded, and leaks an internal invariant message to the user
what_happened: Settings > Equipment Profiles > (profile) > Duplicate > Duplicate, accepting the pre-filled name. The app reported: 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 5 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' The duplicate had in fact succeeded -- equipment_profiles gained row 5 and the profile list in the same screen shows it (three rows: 'Local Work Do Not Lose' [Active], 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)', 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)'). So the message is false in both halves: the operation did not fail, and profile 5 is not absent from the list. It reads like a post-write assertion racing the provider refresh, and the assertion text -- which names a row id and an internal list -- is shown verbatim to the user.
expected: Report success, or if the refresh really has not landed, retry/await it rather than declaring failure. A user who believes this message will press Duplicate again and end up with a third copy.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > select a profile > overflow > Duplicate > press Duplicate. (I hit it on the second duplicate of the same source profile, i.e. when the proposed name collided with an existing profile.) sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' shows the new row; the list in the UI shows it too.
evidence: tree: 'panel: Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 5 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' alongside DB rows 3,4,5 and a list rendering all three.
where: the duplicate handler in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_controls.dart and the profiles notifier's post-duplicate lookup
location_wrong: Cited 'the duplicate handler in .../profile_controls.dart'. Both the handler and the message live in .../equipment_profiles_screen_parts/screen_shell.dart -- _duplicateProfile at :362-396, the throw in _awaitMutatedProfile at :311-324, the snackbar at :394. profile_controls.dart holds unrelated widgets (_EditableFilterChip, _DeviceChip).
proposed_fix: Await the refreshed state (or look the row up by id in the DAO result) before asserting; never surface a Bad state message as user copy.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live, 3 times out of 5 duplicates of the same source profile. Duplicates 1 and 2 succeeded silently; 3, 4 and 5 each raised the snackbar 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 4 / 5 / 6 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' while sqlite3 showed rows 4, 5 and 6 present and the list in the same screen rendered all of them (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-31.png). Both halves of the message are false exactly as claimed. It is a post-write refresh race: screen_shell.dart:311-324 _awaitMutatedProfile awaits ref.read(equipmentProfilesProvider.future) after duplicateProfile's ref.invalidateSelf() and throws a StateError when the id is not yet in the returned list; that assertion text goes straight to showErrorSnackBar at :394.

title: The 'default startup profile' that Settings > General promises has no UI anywhere -- it is pinned to whichever profile you created first
what_happened: Settings > General > Auto-connect equipment reads 'Connects the default startup profile on launch, falling back to the last active profile when no default is set'. Equipment Profiles has no notion of a default: the badge says 'Active', the header action says 'Set Active', and the overflow menu is Edit / Duplicate / Export / Delete. Nothing shows or sets a default. In the database equipment_profiles.is_default is set on whichever profile was created first and never moves: after I created a profile (is_default=1), duplicated it twice (both is_default=0) and pressed Set Active on a duplicate, the rows read 3|...|is_active=0|is_default=1, 4|...|is_active=1|is_default=0. So the rig the app says it will connect on launch is not the rig the operator just made active, and there is no screen where that can be seen, let alone changed.
expected: Either show and let the user set the default (a 'Set as default startup profile' item in the overflow, and a 'Default' badge in the list), or drop the concept and make auto-connect use the active profile -- which is what the operator will assume.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > create a profile, duplicate it, select the copy and press Set Active. sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select id,name,is_active,is_default from equipment_profiles' -> is_default is still on the original. Search all of Settings for 'default profile': the only hit is the General page's description text.
evidence: DB rows quoted above; Equipment Profiles tree showing only 'Active' / 'Set Active' and the four-item overflow menu; General settings copy captured in the tree.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/ (no default affordance) vs the auto-connect description in the general settings section
proposed_fix: Add a 'Set as default' action and a Default badge, and show which profile auto-connect will use on the General page.
verdict_reasoning: All three parts reproduced live. (1) Settings > General still reads 'Auto-connect equipment / Connects the default startup profile on launch, falling back to the last active profile when no default is set'. (2) Equipment Profiles exposes no default affordance: badge 'Active', header action 'Set Active', overflow exactly Edit / Duplicate / Export / Delete (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-21.png). (3) The flag does not follow activation: after creating profile 1 (is_active=1, is_default=1), duplicating it five times (all is_default=0) and pressing Set Active on profile 2, sqlite3 shows 1|is_active=0|is_default=1 and 2|is_active=1|is_default=0. So the rig the copy says will be connected on launch is not the one just activated, and no screen can see or change it. (Separate observation, not part of this claim: grep finds no consumer of autoConnectEquipment in any startup connect path at all.)
